question: A newborn infant presents with fragile skin, developing cutaneous bullae and denuded epidermal areas following gentle handling. Biopsy reveals subepidermal cleavage at the basement membrane zone. A mutation affecting which basement membrane structure is responsible for this condition?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Type I collagen is a fibrillar collagen found in skin, tendon, bone, and fascia that provides high tensile strength, but it does not form the anchoring fibrils of the dermo-epidermal junction. Dysfunction would result in osteogenesis imperfecta or connective tissue laxity, not subepidermal blistering from lost basement membrane adhesion.
Type III collagen forms reticular fibers in organs, uterus, and blood vessels, as well as the reticular lamina. It is not mutated in epidermolysis bullosa to cause defective anchoring fibrils.

Type IV collagen is non-fibrillar and forms the meshwork of the lamina densa within the basal lamina. While vital to basement membrane architecture, it does not form the anchoring fibrils that hold the basement membrane to the dermis.

Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) is caused by mutations in the collagen type VII gene, which forms dysfunctional anchoring fibrils. These fibrils normally anchor the basement membrane to the underlying dermis, so their failure leads to subepidermal blistering under minimal mechanical force.
Type II collagen is found primarily in cartilage, nucleus pulposus, and vitreous body, not in the dermo-epidermal junction.

question: A 28-year-old man presents with well-demarcated depigmented macules and patches on his hands and wrists. Histologic evaluation of the depigmented lesions demonstrates a complete absence of cells containing melanosomes within the stratum basale. Which cell type is primarily affected in this condition?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the function of the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, and Merkel cells.

options.rationale: Langerhans cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells residing primarily in the stratum spinosum; they do not synthesize melanin or melanosomes and are unaffected in vitiligo.
Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition characterized by the destruction and absence of melanocytes in the stratum basale, leading to loss of melanosome synthesis and depigmented patches.
Merkel cells are neuroendocrine mechanoreceptors located in the stratum basale that perceive touch; they do not synthesize pigment.
Keratinocytes receive melanin from melanocytes via dendritic processes, but they are not the cells lost or destroyed in vitiligo.
Fibroblasts reside in the dermis and synthesize extracellular collagen and elastic fibers, not melanosomes.

question: A 45-year-old man presents with superficial erosions and crusted lesions across his upper trunk. Biopsy reveals intraepidermal blister formation with loss of cell-to-cell adhesion between surface keratinocytes due to autoantibodies against desmoglein-1. Dysfunction of which junctional structure is responsible for this patient's findings?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: Hemidesmosomes attach basal keratinocytes to the underlying basement membrane. Autoantibodies against hemidesmosomal proteins cause subepidermal blistering (bullous pemphigoid), whereas pemphigus foliaceus involves superficial desmosomes.
Tight junctions form apical diffusion barriers in epithelia but are not targeted by desmoglein-1 autoantibodies.
Lamellar bodies secrete lipid substances to render the stratum corneum water-repellent; they are not cellular adhesion complexes targeted in pemphigus foliaceus.
Keratohyalin granules contain filaggrin within the stratum granulosum and do not participate in cell-to-cell adhesion mediated by desmoglein.

Pemphigus foliaceus involves autoantibodies against desmoglein-1, a constituent of desmosomes located near the top of the epidermis. Disruption of desmosomal cell-to-cell adhesion causes surface keratinocytes to detach and form superficial blisters.

question: A musician relies on precise perception of high-frequency rapid vibrations (200 Hz) applied to his fingertips during performances. Which sensory receptor is primarily responsible for transducing this specific modality?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Pacinian corpuscles are fast-adapting encapsulated receptors situated in deep skin and subcutis that specialize in detecting rapid vibration (approximately 200 Hz) and deep pressure.
Free nerve endings lack capsules and transduce pain, temperature, itch, and crude touch, not high-frequency vibration.
Meissner corpuscles are fast-adapting receptors in the papillary dermis that respond best to low-frequency vibration (10-50 Hz) and light touch.
Merkel cell-neurite complexes are slow-adapting receptors that sense sustained touch, pressure, and texture.
Ruffini corpuscles are slow-adapting receptors located in the dermis that respond specifically to skin stretch.

question: A 16-year-old male presents with open and closed comedones, erythematous papules, and pustules on his face. The pathophysiologic mechanism involves hyperkeratinization and sebum accumulation leading to follicle obstruction and rupture. Which unit is directly obstructed in this condition?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: Eccrine glands produce watery sweat directly onto the epidermal surface for thermoregulation and are not involved in comedone formation.
Apocrine glands produce odoriferous secretions in specific axillary and perianal regions and do not form facial comedones.
Acne vulgaris is caused by clogging of the pilosebaceous orifice by a keratotic plug and sebum, leading to cystic dilation, follicle rupture, and subsequent inflammation.
Glomus bodies are arteriovenous shunts involved in dermal thermoregulation, not glandular secretion or acne.
Vascular plexuses supply blood flow to the skin but do not contain sebaceous or keratinized follicular ducts.

question: A skin biopsy from a patient with contact dermatitis demonstrates intraepidermal dendritic cells containing distinctive tennis-racket shaped cytoplasmic organelles under electron microscopy. What is the primary function of these cells?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the function of the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, and Merkel cells.

options.rationale: Melanin synthesis and transfer are functions of melanocytes via melanosomes, not Langerhans cells.
Langerhans cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells residing in the epidermis (most prominent in the stratum spinosum) characterized by tennis-racket shaped Birbeck granules.
Tactile sensation is transduced by Merkel cells and sensory nerve endings, not Langerhans cells.
Vitamin D synthesis is performed by keratinocytes upon exposure to UV light.
Collagen secretion is carried out by dermal fibroblasts, not Langerhans cells.

question: A 4-year-old child with severe atopic dermatitis is found to have a loss-of-function mutation in the gene encoding filaggrin. In which layer of the epidermis is this protein normally stored within basophilic granules?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: The stratum basale contains proliferating cuboidal stem cells and melanocytes; it does not contain keratohyalin granules containing profilaggrin.
The stratum spinosum contains polyhedral cells with prominent desmosomal spines, but lacks mature basophilic keratohyalin granules.

The stratum granulosum contains keratinocytes packed with basophilic keratohyalin granules. Profilaggrin/filaggrin is a primary component of these granules and is essential for skin barrier formation.
The stratum lucidum is a clear, thin layer of dead keratinocytes found only in thick skin; keratohyalin granules disappear as cells enter this layer.
The stratum corneum consists of flattened, non-nucleated dead cornified cells where filaggrin has already processed keratin filament alignment.

question: An individual exposed to sudden freezing temperatures undergoes cutaneous thermoregulation to minimize core heat loss. Specialized arteriovenous shunts located in the dermis of the fingertips contract, diverting blood away from the skin surface. What are these structures called?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: Meissner corpuscles are sensory touch receptors in dermal papillae, not arteriovenous shunts.
Pacinian corpuscles are sensory mechanoreceptors for vibration, not vascular shunts.
Eccrine ducts transport sweat to the skin surface for evaporative cooling, not blood flow diversion.
Apocrine glands secrete viscous odor-producing fluid into hair follicles, not blood.

Glomus bodies are specialized arteriovenous shunts surrounded by connective tissue in the dermis of peripheral sites (fingertips, feet, ears). They divert blood away from the surface when cold to retain heat.

question: An athlete running in high ambient heat relies on watery sweat production for evaporative body cooling. Histology of the palmar skin reveals simple tubular glands discharging sweat directly onto the skin surface via an acrosyringium. Which gland type is performing this function?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: Eccrine glands are merocrine sweat glands distributed widely across skin (especially thick skin) that secrete watery sweat directly onto the surface for thermoregulation.
Sebaceous glands release oily sebum into hair follicles via holocrine secretion, not watery sweat onto open skin.
Apocrine glands produce lipid- and protein-rich odoriferous secretions into hair follicles in limited body regions (axilla, groin).
Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine glands in the external ear canal that produce earwax.
Mammary glands are modified apocrine glands specialized for milk production.

question: A neurological examination demonstrates impaired light touch discrimination in a patient's fingertips, whereas deep pressure perception remains completely intact. Biopsy of the dermal papillae reveals loss of encapsulated tactile structures. Which receptor type is damaged?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Pacinian corpuscles are located deep in the dermis/subcutis and detect rapid vibration and deep pressure, which remained intact in this patient.
Meissner corpuscles are fast-adapting encapsulated receptors located specifically within papillary dermal papillae that mediate light discriminatory touch.
Merkel cells reside in the basal layer of the epidermis (not encapsulated in dermal papillae) and act as slow-adapting touch receptors.
Ruffini corpuscles respond to tissue stretch in the deep dermis, not light touch in dermal papillae.
Free nerve endings are unencapsulated fibers that detect pain and temperature throughout the skin.

question: Cross-sectional histology of a hair follicle reveals an inner epithelial layer containing prominent, coarse eosinophilic keratohyalin granules. To which layers of the surface epidermis does this internal root sheath loosely correspond?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: The stratum basale and spinosum loosely correspond to the external root sheath (ERS), not the internal root sheath.
The stratum spinosum corresponds to the ERS, while the stratum granulosum corresponds to the IRS.
The internal root sheath (IRS) of the hair follicle contains coarse eosinophilic keratohyalin granules and loosely corresponds to the stratum granulosum and stratum corneum of the epidermis.
The stratum basale corresponds to the ERS and does not contain keratohyalin granules.
The stratum basale forms the proliferative pool corresponding to the ERS.

question: A deep surgical excision specimen reveals a layer located beneath the reticular dermis composed primarily of lobules of mature adipocytes partitioned by fibrous connective tissue septa. What is a key physiological function of this layer?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: Cholecalciferol synthesis occurs in epidermal keratinocytes exposed to light, not in subcutaneous adipose tissue.
Melanin synthesis occurs in epidermal melanocytes.
Antigen presentation is performed by Langerhans cells in the epidermis and superficial dermis.

The subcutis (hypodermis/panniculus) is composed of mature adipose tissue separated by collagenous septa. Its primary functions include energy/triglyceride storage, thermal insulation, and structural padding.
Light touch perception is mediated by tactile corpuscles and Merkel cells in the upper skin layers.

question: Transmission electron microscopy of the dermo-epidermal basement membrane reveals an electron-dense layer situated directly beneath the lamina lucida. Which collagen type forms the principal structural meshwork of this lamina densa layer?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Type I collagen forms thick fibrillar bundles in the dermis, bone, and tendon, but does not form the lamina densa meshwork.
Type II collagen is found in cartilage and vitreous body.
Type III collagen forms reticular fibers and constitutes the reticular lamina below the lamina densa.
The lamina densa of the basal lamina is primarily composed of non-fibrillar Type IV collagen that creates a sheet-like supporting barrier.
Type VII collagen forms anchoring fibrils extending from the basal lamina into the papillary dermis.

question: A patient with limited sun exposure is evaluated for bone density loss. In the epidermis, which cell type expresses vitamin D receptors and directly synthesizes cholecalciferol upon exposure to ultraviolet radiation?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the function of the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, and Merkel cells.

options.rationale: Langerhans cells function as antigen-presenting immune cells and do not synthesize vitamin D.
Melanocytes produce melanin to protect against UV radiation; they do not synthesize cholecalciferol.
Keratinocytes are the predominant epidermal cell type, possess vitamin D receptors, and synthesize vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) when exposed to ultraviolet light.
Merkel cells are neuroendocrine mechanoreceptors for touch.
Fibroblasts reside in the dermis and synthesize extracellular collagen and elastic fibers.

question: An individual walking outside on a chilly day experiences sudden piloerection ('goose bumps'). This involuntary response is caused by sympathetic stimulation of which tissue attached to hair follicles?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: The arrector pili muscle is composed of involuntary smooth muscle attached to the hair follicle. Sympathetic activation causes contraction, raising the hair shaft and expressing adjacent sebaceous glands.
Arrector pili muscles are involuntary smooth muscle, not voluntary somatic skeletal muscle.
Cardiac muscle is localized exclusively to the myocardium.
Connective tissue sheaths surround follicles, but active contraction is mediated by smooth muscle fibers.
Subcutaneous fat provides insulation and padding, lacking contractile machinery.

question: Keratinocytes undergo continuous mitotic division in the basal layer followed by progressive upward displacement through the epidermal strata. What is the normal transit time for a basal cell to reach the stratum corneum?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: Two days is far too short for complete epidermal maturation and cornification.
Seven days represents only half of the transit time required to enter the stratum corneum.
Ten days is shorter than the standard two-week maturation window.
Twenty days exceeds the standard transit time to reach the stratum corneum, though total turnover including shedding is 28 days.

The normal transit time for a keratinocyte to migrate from the stratum basale to the stratum corneum is two weeks (14 days); cells are then shed two weeks after reaching the stratum corneum for a total 28-day cycle.

question: Fibroblasts in the dermis synthesize a specific fibrillar collagen that provides high tensile strength to skin, tendon, bone, and fascia. This protein constitutes approximately 90% of total body collagen. Which collagen type is this?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Type I collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body (90% of total collagen), forming strong 67 nm fibrils in skin, tendon, bone, dentin, and fascia.
Type II collagen forms fibrils in cartilage, vitreous body, and cornea.
Type III collagen forms thin reticular fibers in blood vessels, uterus, and lymphoid organs.
Type IV collagen is non-fibrillar and forms basal laminae.
Type VII collagen forms small anchoring fibrils in basal laminae.

question: Comparing skin specimens from light-skinned and dark-skinned individuals reveals marked variations in epidermal melanin content. Which statement accurately describes the cellular basis for this physiological difference?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the function of the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, and Merkel cells.

options.text: Dark skin contains more total melanocytes
options.rationale: The number of melanocytes is similar between light- and dark-skinned individuals.

options.text: Dark skin synthesizes more melanin pigment
options.rationale: While the total number of melanocytes is similar across skin types, dark-skinned individuals synthesize more melanin pigment within their melanosomes.

options.text: Light skin lacks extensive dendritic processes
options.rationale: Melanocytes in all individuals possess dendritic processes to transfer melanosomes to surrounding keratinocytes.

options.text: Light skin produces melanin without tyrosine
options.rationale: Melanin synthesis in all humans requires the amino acid tyrosine within melanosomes.

options.text: Dark skin completely lacks stratum basale
options.rationale: All human skin possesses a stratum basale layer where melanocytes reside.

question: Histologic sectioning of thick glabrous skin from the palm reveals a distinct clear band termed the stratum lucidum. Which characteristic describes the cell layer forming this zone?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: Mitotic proliferation occurs in the stratum basale, not in the clear, dead stratum lucidum.
The stratum lucidum ('clear layer') is present only in thick skin and consists of 3 to 5 layers of dead, flattened, non-nucleated keratinocytes.
Langerhans cells are most prominent in the stratum spinosum.
Merkel cells reside in the stratum basale.
Basophilic keratohyalin granules define the stratum granulosum, which lies immediately beneath the stratum lucidum.

question: Cutaneous mechanoreceptors vary in adaptation rate and anatomical location. Which unit functions specifically as a slow-adapting receptor for discriminatory touch and pressure located in the basal layer of the epidermis?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Meissner corpuscles are fast-adapting encapsulated touch receptors in papillary dermal papillae.
Pacinian corpuscles are fast-adapting deep pressure and vibration receptors.
Merkel cell-neurite complexes are slow-adapting touch and pressure receptors situated in the basal epidermis.
Ruffini corpuscles are slow-adapting stretch receptors in the dermis.
Free nerve endings detect pain, temperature, and itch.

question: Exocrine glands of the skin are classified by their mode of secretion and anatomical distribution. Which structures represent modified specialized apocrine glands?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: Sebaceous glands are holocrine glands that secrete sebum.
Eccrine glands are merocrine sweat glands; glomus bodies are vascular arteriovenous shunts.
Meibomian glands are modified sebaceous holocrine glands.
Thyroid and adrenal glands are endocrine glands, not skin adnexal glands.
Apocrine glands are odor-producing glands in the axillae and groin; modified apocrine glands include ceruminous glands (earwax) and mammary glands (milk).

question: Dermal mast cells play a key role in immediate hypersensitivity reactions through degranulation and histamine release. Which histological stain is utilized to highlight the metachromatic cytoplasmic granules of mast cells?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) routinely stains cytoplasm pink, making mast cell granules inconspicuous.
Toluidine blue (or Giemsa) is a special metachromatic stain used to visualize the dark purple cytoplasmic granules of mast cells and basophils.
Masson trichrome stains collagen fibers blue/green, not mast cell granules.
PAS stains glycogen and basement membrane carbohydrates magenta.
Verhoeff van Gieson stains elastic fibers black.

question: Keratinocytes in the stratum granulosum contain specialized membrane-bound organelles called lamellar bodies (Odland bodies). What is the primary function of the lipid contents released by these organelles?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: Melanin synthesis is performed by melanocytes in melanosomes.
Mitotic stem cell division occurs in the stratum basale.
Touch transmission is performed by Merkel cells and sensory nerve receptors.
Type VII collagen is formed by fibroblasts/keratinocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction, not within lamellar bodies.
Lamellar bodies (keratinosomes, Odland bodies) in the stratum granulosum secrete a lipid substance that coats keratin flakes, rendering the stratum corneum water-repellent.

question: The dermis consists of two layers with an indistinct anatomical boundary. Which feature distinguishes the superficial papillary dermis from the underlying reticular dermis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: The deeper reticular dermis contacts the subcutis, whereas the papillary dermis contacts the epidermis.
Thick, coarse collagen bundles are characteristic of the deeper reticular dermis.
Adipocytes predominate in the subcutis layer.
The papillary dermis is the most superficial dermal layer, forming dermal papillae in direct contact with the interfollicular epidermis.
The papillary dermis contains a rich superficial capillary plexus supplying the epidermis.

question: Concentric sectioning of a hair shaft reveals distinct epithelial and keratinized layers. Which layer forms the outermost boundary of the hair shaft itself, consisting of overlapping, shingle-like flat cells?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.rationale: The cuticle forms the outermost layer of the hair shaft and consists of a single overlapping layer of flat keratinized cells arranged like shingles.
The medulla forms the central core of the hair shaft.
The cortex lies between the medulla and cuticle, containing densely packed keratinized cells with pigment granules.
The internal root sheath surrounds the hair shaft within the follicle but is not part of the shaft proper.
The external root sheath forms the outer wall of the follicle continuous with the basal epidermis.

question: Systematic evaluation of dermal sensory innervation identifies several specialized encapsulated corpuscles. Which receptor responds primarily to mechanical stretching of cutaneous connective tissue?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Pacinian corpuscles detect high-frequency vibration and rapid pressure changes.
Meissner corpuscles detect light touch and low-frequency flutter.
Merkel cells detect sustained touch and surface texture.
Ruffini corpuscles (bulbous corpuscles) are slow-adapting dermal receptors that transduce skin stretch.
Free nerve endings perceive pain, temperature, itch, and crude touch.

question: What are the three primary anatomical layers that constitute human skin?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: Corneum, spinosum, and basale are sub-layers of the epidermis, not the three primary layers of skin.
Papillary and reticular are layers of the dermis; adventitia is an outer vascular vessel wall layer.
The skin is composed of three component layers: the superficial epidermis, the intermediate dermis, and the deep subcutis (hypodermis).
Epithelium, lamina propria, and submucosa define mucous membrane architecture, not cutaneous skin layers.
Cuticle, cortex, and medulla are layers of a hair shaft, not the primary layers of skin.

question: Which cell type represents the predominant, most numerous cell in the stratified squamous epithelium of the human epidermis?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the function of the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, and Merkel cells.

options.rationale: Fibroblasts are the main cell type of the connective tissue dermis, not the epidermis.
Melanocytes are scattered basally in the epidermis but are far less numerous than keratinocytes.
Langerhans cells constitute a minor population of dendritic immune cells in the epidermis.
Keratinocytes are the predominant cell type of the epidermis, proliferating in the base and forming a keratinized surface layer.
Merkel cells are sparse neuroendocrine tactile cells found in the basal layer.

question: Which collagen type specifically forms the anchoring fibrils that secure the epidermal basement membrane to the underlying papillary dermis?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Type I collagen forms thick dermal collagen bundles providing tensile strength.
Type III collagen forms reticular fibers in the reticular lamina.
Type IV collagen forms the lamina densa meshwork of the basal lamina.
Type XI collagen is a fibrillar collagen associated with cartilage matrix.
Type VII collagen forms the small anchoring fibrils that tie the basal lamina of the basement membrane to the underlying dermis.

question: Which set of anatomical structures collectively constitutes a complete pilosebaceous unit?
cited_learning_objective: Identify and describe the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, arrector pili muscles, and pilosebaceous units.

options.text: Hair follicle, arrector pili, sebaceous gland
options.rationale: A pilosebaceous unit is defined as a hair follicle, its associated arrector pili muscle, and its associated sebaceous gland.

options.text: Hair follicle, eccrine gland, apocrine gland
options.rationale: Eccrine sweat glands open onto free skin surface and are independent of the pilosebaceous unit.

options.text: Arrector pili, glomus body, Meissner corpuscle
options.rationale: Glomus bodies and Meissner corpuscles are vascular and sensory dermal structures, respectively.

options.text: Sebaceous gland, eccrine duct, Pacinian corpuscle
options.rationale: Eccrine ducts and Pacinian corpuscles do not form part of a hair follicle complex.

options.text: Hair follicle, sweat pore, subcutaneous fat
options.rationale: Sweat pores belong to eccrine glands; subcutaneous fat belongs to the hypodermis.
